contentBlocks.text: This week you wrote a complete Punjabi opinion piece from scratch. Let's review it all!

Quick review: ਵਿਚਾਰ (opinion) writing differs from ਖ਼ਬਰ (news) writing by expressing a personal stance (Day 1). A strong ਪੱਖ (stance) is clear and specific (Day 2). ਦਲੀਲ (reasoning) supports the stance with real reasons (Day 3). You wrote a complete piece with a ਸੱਦਾ (call to action) (Day 4). Explain in your own words why a clear stance, real reasoning, and a specific call to action together make an opinion piece genuinely persuasive.
Great work this week — you wrote a complete, persuasive Punjabi opinion piece from scratch! Next week we'll build on these skills with something new.

objectives: Review the opinion-vs-news distinction, stance, reasoning, and call to action
Explain why these three elements together make an opinion piece genuinely persuasive
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child explain why the three elements together create persuasion.
3. Complete the review worksheet.
4. Celebrate finishing a full week of Punjabi opinion writing!
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just the skill the child found hardest this week (often writing specific reasons) rather than requiring an even summary of all three
Ready for more: ask the child how this week's opinion-writing skills connect to Grade 10's formal-essay structure
This is a good checkpoint to note which of the week's three opinion-writing elements needs the most reinforcement going forward
teacherGuide.answerKey: A clear stance tells the reader exactly what position is being argued, real reasoning gives them something concrete to actually consider and be convinced by, and a specific call to action tells them exactly what to do with that conviction — together, these three elements move a reader from simply understanding an opinion to genuinely being persuaded and knowing how to act on it.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates this week's advanced-composition thread before the course continues, matching the established Day-5-review pacing used across every unit this session.

generationData.instructions: Answer to review this week's opinion-writing skills.
